lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Clarify the target role.
items.because: The resume presents three different profiles and the most recent job is mechanical, which may confuse the reader about your intended direction.

items.says: Fix the experience order.
items.because: The Harbor Payments internship ended after the Crestline role, so it should appear above Crestline in reverse-chronological order.

items.says: Reduce responsibility-only bullets.
items.because: Several bullets describe what you did but not what changed as a result; stronger bullets include measurable outcomes.

items.says: Remove duplicated evidence in Harbor Payments section.
items.because: Multiple bullets cover the checkout A/B test and roadmap prioritization, leading to overlap.

items.says: Make the product/operations target explicit so the diesel mechanic role does not dominate the reader’s interpretation.
items.because: The current role is not aligned with product management and may distract from your intended positioning.

items.says: Confirm that the graduation date accurately reflects completion.
items.because: Since the date has passed, do not leave ambiguity about whether the degree is completed.

items.says: Add a concentration, relevant coursework, or academic distinction only if it directly supports the target role.
items.because: This can strengthen the education section if relevant.

items.says: Clarify whether the under-five-day figure is an average, maximum, or target, and whether it represents an improvement over a prior baseline.
items.because: The metric is ambiguous and may overstate your impact.

items.says: Avoid implying sole attribution for the turnaround result unless you can support it.
items.because: You should not claim sole credit for a team result without evidence.

items.says: Add the operational result if available: inspection pass rate, avoided downtime, reduced repeat failures, improved compliance, or number of systems/vessels covered.
items.because: The bullet is currently too responsibility-focused and lacks impact.

items.says: Connect 'logged service records' to audit readiness, regulatory compliance, maintenance planning, or reliability.
items.because: Logging records is low-impact unless tied to a business result.

items.says: Add the scale: number of carriers, managers, lanes, or regions covered.
items.because: The bullet lacks context and outcome.

items.says: Explain what decisions the scorecards or review meeting enabled, such as corrective actions, carrier changes, service improvements, or cost reductions.
items.because: The bullet lacks a measurable outcome.

items.says: Consider removing this bullet if there was no measurable outcome, as the other Crestline bullets are stronger.
items.because: It is weaker than your other evidence.

items.says: Specify whether the 30% is a relative reduction or a reduction in percentage points.
items.because: The metric is ambiguous.

items.says: Add the baseline error rate or operational consequence if available.
items.because: This would clarify the impact of the improvement.

items.says: Clarify how forecast error was measured, such as the specific error metric or product scope.
items.because: The metric is currently vague.

items.says: Be precise about the change from 18% to 11%; this is a seven-percentage-point reduction and a 38.9% relative reduction.
items.because: The improvement should be described accurately.

items.says: Ensure the 12-quarter duration reflects your actual ownership period, not just the process existence.
items.because: This avoids overstating your role.

items.says: Split this bullet into separate accomplishments or remove the least relevant component for the target role.
items.because: It currently contains too many separate actions and is hard to scan.

items.says: Add the financial value of the 1,800 annual driver hours saved if you can calculate it credibly.
items.because: This would strengthen the business impact.

items.says: Include the contract savings, improved terms, implementation result, or other measurable consequence from vendor negotiations.
items.because: 'Taking over vendor negotiations' describes an action but not an outcome.

items.says: Clarify whether the time-to-first-payment reduction was statistically or operationally significant and whether the pilot led to a broader rollout.
items.because: The impact and follow-up are unclear.

items.says: Ensure the relationship between the pilot and later rollout is clear and not repetitive with other bullets.
items.because: There is potential overlap with the presentation bullet.

items.says: Clarify the experiment population and whether the result was statistically significant.
items.because: The scope and rigor of the result are unclear.

items.says: Distinguish between the pilot/test population and the later all-merchant rollout.
items.because: The rollout scope is ambiguous.

items.says: Be precise that this is a five-percentage-point increase, not necessarily a 5% increase.
items.because: The metric should be described accurately.

items.says: The definition of Reach as the number of support tickets a feature would close is not the standard meaning in RICE; clarify if this was a proxy and ensure all RICE components were applied.
items.because: This may misrepresent your understanding of the framework.

items.says: State the decision or result produced by the prioritization, not just the framework used.
items.because: Naming a framework alone is not strong evidence of product judgment.

items.says: Combine this evidence with the roadmap result or remove one of the two bullets to avoid overlap.
items.because: This bullet overlaps with the roadmap-prioritization bullet.

items.says: Add the business consequence of the work: projected loss reduction, expected support reduction, selected initiative, or executive decision.
items.because: The impact is not stated.

items.says: Reduce the number of intermediate steps and emphasize the decision and impact.
items.because: The sequence of activities is long and process-heavy.

items.says: Remove this bullet or use it only if you need to demonstrate experimental design rigor, as it is redundant with the earlier checkout-conversion bullet.
items.because: It repeats evidence already given.

items.says: Clarify the experiment's sample size, confidence or significance information, and the actual unit of analysis.
items.because: The current wording is confusing and lacks rigor.

items.says: Make the scope of the funded rollout more concrete: timeline, number of merchants, regions, or expected business impact.
items.because: The impact of the presentation is not fully clear.

items.says: Ensure the distinction between execution and organizational adoption is clear to avoid overlap with the onboarding bullet.
items.because: There is slight overlap with the first onboarding bullet.

items.says: Clarify what 'to 3,100 students' means: total eligible audience, registered users, reached audience, or active users.
items.because: The scale is ambiguous.

items.says: Explain how the nine-tonne figure was measured if it is an estimate.
items.because: The metric may be an estimate and needs clarification.

items.says: Make the measurement period for 'in its first year' explicit, since the project is ongoing and began in October 2023.
items.because: The time frame is unclear.

items.says: Correct the percentage calculation: the increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: Accuracy matters because hiring managers often check obvious calculations.

items.says: Clarify whether the reminders were the tested cause of the full increase or just one product change associated with it.
items.because: Causality is not established.

items.says: If you have retention, notification engagement, repeat pickup, or cohort data, include it to make the product impact more credible than a simple before-and-after comparison.
items.because: This would strengthen the evidence of impact.

items.says: Correct the percentage terminology: 75% to 95% is a 20-percentage-point increase, not a 20% increase.
items.because: Accuracy matters because hiring managers often check obvious calculations.

items.says: Clarify the time period over which this was measured and whether the improvement was sustained.
items.because: The duration and sustainability of the improvement are unclear.

items.says: If the change improved availability, reduced waste, or lowered cancellations, include that outcome if available.
items.because: The operational impact is not stated.

items.says: Clearly distinguish between a modeled opportunity and realized savings.
items.because: 'Sized' signals that the savings were not yet achieved.

items.says: Add the main assumptions or implementation conditions if space allows.
items.because: This would clarify the credibility of the savings estimate.

items.says: Clarify whether you personally led the financial model, operational analysis, stakeholder work, or recommendation process.
items.because: Your specific role is not clear.

items.says: Specify what changed and what evidence showed adoption: reduced form length, shorter intake time, fewer errors, higher completion, or staff implementation.
items.because: The bullet is too passive and vague.

items.says: If there was no measurable result, consider removing this bullet or combining its strongest evidence with the pilot recommendation.
items.because: It lacks a concrete outcome.

items.says: Tie adoption to a concrete operational result or implementation milestone.
items.because: 'With the changes adopted' is not enough by itself.

items.says: Avoid repeating the pilot approval already mentioned in the first bullet unless this bullet adds a distinct leadership or stakeholder-management point.
items.because: There is potential overlap with the first bullet.

items.says: If the pilot had a defined scope, timeline, or success criteria, include that information.
items.because: This would clarify the impact of the recommendation.

items.says: Make sure the first and third bullets do not both claim the same approval outcome without adding different evidence.
items.because: Avoid redundancy.

items.says: 'Requirements writing' is somewhat generic; retain it only if you can demonstrate it through product documentation, acceptance criteria, or delivery work.
items.because: It may not be credible without supporting evidence.

items.says: Match the skills to the job descriptions you are targeting rather than listing every method you have encountered.
items.because: This will make the skills section more relevant.

items.says: The tools list is short for a product or operations candidate; add only tools you have actually used and could discuss in an interview.
items.because: A longer, relevant tools list can strengthen your candidacy.

items.says: If you used tools during the A/B testing, app, S&OP, or route-planning work, make sure those tools appear here when relevant to the target role.
items.because: This would better support your experience claims.

items.says: Do not add tools simply to increase keyword density; unsupported tools can create credibility problems.
items.because: Listing tools you have not used can backfire in interviews.
